segments.text: The goal is the manpage5 password. /manpage/manpage4 is a patched Hunt the Wumpus: when you win, log_winner prints your firstname and lastname through an sprintf into a 256-byte stack buffer.

The patched source shows the bug: fgets reads the name, sscanf splits it with percent-100-s percent-100-s, and sprintf writes ctime plus firstname plus lastname into buf. With a no-space name the second token never matches, so lastname keeps whatever the stack held before - and sprintf writes past the buffer's end.
The disassembly confirms the layout: buf sits at ebp minus 0x100, firstname at ebp minus 0x200, lastname at ebp minus 0x300, and the frame has no stack canary - just leave and ret.

The stale lastname is the key. lastname lives 1300 bytes above getnum's 2048-byte input buffer, which still holds my 1602-byte ROOM# line: the line's bytes from offset 1304 become the lastname string. That makes the sprintf output about 403 bytes - past the saved ebp and the return address at output 260.

The payload: the ROOM# line carries the NOP sled and the return value at line offset 1417, which lands exactly in the return-address slot. The name line carries 52 NOPs plus 48 bytes of shellcode, which sscanf copies into firstname at ebp minus 0x200 - below the overflowed frame, so the return value just has to point into that sled.

The shellcode needs no setresuid: the game is already setuid manpage5, so its euid can read the password file directly. It opens slash-tmp-slash-x - a symlink to the password file created first - reads 100 bytes onto the stack and writes them to file descriptor one. Exit code one marks that the shellcode ran.

One practical discovery: with a pty on stdin the overflow never reaches the return address - the game exits cleanly. Driven through a pipe, the sprintf writes its full output and E I P is hijacked. The exploit feeds the whole game session through a pipe and sweeps the return value from 0xffffc800 to 0xffffdc00 until the process exits with code one - the shellcode's own exit.
The sweep lands at 0xffffd0b8, and the shellcode dumps the password: v2ltdizZfm.
Level four solved - the login as manpage5 works.
